newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians, Israelis welcome EU peace envoy.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians, Israelis welcome EU peace envoy.

text.p: Palestinians and Israelis on Wednesday welcomed the European Union's appointment of a special envoy to the Middle East.

The European Union on Monday named Spanish diplomat Miguel Angel Moratinos to the post. Diplomats said he was given a mandate to observe the peace process, establish relations with Israeli and Palestinian negotiators and report on possible action the EU might take.
"The Palestinian people, the PLO and the PNA (Palestinian National Authority) warmly welcome the appointment of this able ambassador," the Palestinian Information Ministry said.
It said in a statement it hoped Moratinos would help "resuce the faltering peace process".
Israeli Foreign Ministry spokesman Danny Shek also expressed satisfaction over the appointment of Moratinos, Spain's ambassador in Israel.
Right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the United States, the main broker in peace talks with the PLO, have been cool to a European role.

"Israel was satisfied that the decision of the EU took into consideration Israel's concerns, namely that the envoy should have the role of monitoring and reporting about the peace process and would not be directly involved in the substance of the negotiations," Shek told Reuters.

Moratinos told Radio France International on Tuesday he intended to act as a political go-between, provide economic aid and calm a heated atmosphere rather than push a French bid for an EU seat at peace talks.
"I believe one sits around the negotiating table only when one is invited to do so by all the parties," he said.
Spain served as the host of a 1991 Middle East peace conference that launched direct Israeli-Arab negotiations.

The peace talks led to Israel-PLO deals on interim Palestinian self-rule and a peace treaty with Jordan. Israel and the PLO are currently negotiating the implementation of an Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Israel's talks with Syria and Lebanon are frozen.
Under France's urging, the 15-nation EU, which has been the chief financial backer of the peace process, has been seeking to play a greater role in the talks.
